title: Chemical short-range order increases the phonon heat conductivity in a refractory high-entropy alloy

recollection.starting_material: Guess: A refractory high‐entropy alloy based on a system of multiple refractory metals (e.g., Nb, Mo, W, Ta, etc.) in a solid solution.
recollection.intervention: Guess: The researchers applied a thermal treatment or controlled processing to deliberately induce chemical short‐range order within the alloy.
recollection.structure: Guess: The material evolved to exhibit regions of local chemical ordering (short‐range order) embedded in an otherwise disordered atomic matrix.
recollection.mechanism: Guess: The presence of chemical short‐range order reduces phonon scattering by creating more coherent atomic arrangements, thus facilitating improved phonon transport.
recollection.results: Guess: Quantitatively, the study reported a significant increase in phonon heat conductivity (for example, an improvement on the order of 15–30% relative to the fully random configuration), though exact numbers are not recalled.

score.note: The intervention and structure are only generic restatements of inducing SRO, with the proposed thermal treatment not matching the Monte Carlo intervention and no mention of B2-like HfTi/TiZr clusters or percolation. The reduced-scattering mechanism is directionally correct and goes beyond the title, though it omits reduced lattice distortion, percolative pathways, and phonon-DOS changes. The guessed 15–30% increase is not close to the reported ~12%.
